extracted.intended_audience: ERC peer reviewers (Panel Chairs, Panel Members, Panel Evaluators, Remote Referees) for Starting and Consolidator Grant calls
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation rules for experts performing individual and panel-based peer review of ERC Starting and Consolidator Grant proposals under Horizon Europe, covering the two-step evaluation, scoring, conflicts of interest, review quality and budget assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence is the sole evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of proposals is based on a panel-based, peer review evaluation with excellence as the sole criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All assessments on proposals must be made against the evaluation criterion and its detailed elements alone. No other criteria than the evaluation elements defined in the ERC Work Programme must be considered; incorrect application of the criterion is a procedural error that may justify re-evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Step 1 questions (Part I / Part B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 1 reviewers assess: 'To what extent does the research address important scientific questions?' and 'To what extent are the project’s objectives ambitious and will it advance the frontier of knowledge?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part I (Part B1) should present envisaged research, lay out the current state of knowledge, explain the scientific question and objectives, and present the overall approach or research strategy. It forms the basis for deciding whether the proposal proceeds to Step 2; all essential information must be covered in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Project — Step 2 questions (Part II / Part B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 2 reviewers assess the Step 1 questions and additionally: 'To what extent are the research methodology and working arrangements appropriate to achieve the goals of the project?' and 'To what extent are the timescales and resources adequate and properly justified?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part II should be a detailed explanation of project implementation, including research methodology, work plan, risk assessment and mitigating measures, justification for requested budget and resources, and any further necessary background not included in Part I. Budget/resource assessment is performed at Step 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator assessment (Step 1 & Step 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual capacity and creativity of the Principal Investigator is assessed by: 'To what extent has the PI demonstrated the ability to conduct groundbreaking research?', 'To what extent does the PI provide evidence of creative and original thinking?', and 'To what extent does the PI have the required scientific expertise and capacity to successfully execute the project?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should focus on scientific content of achievements, may consider preprints (with DOI), and take into account career stage, career breaks, major life events and diverse research career paths. Avoid references to PI's age, nationality, gender, or Host Institution standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical mark for the Research Project (proposal mark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers award an overall numerical mark for the Research Project ranging from 5 (Outstanding), 4 (Excellent), 3 (Very Good), 2 (Good) to 1 (Non-competitive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks may be awarded in integers or halves; use of the full range of marks is recommended. The proposal numerical mark should be consistent with the explanatory comments. Proposal marks are not communicated to applicants (only final panel score is).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative overall assessment for the Principal Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers give an overall qualitative assessment for the PI using five options: Outstanding / Excellent / Very Good / Good / Non-competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The qualitative PI assessment should be consistent with the PI comments. At Step 2 an explanatory comment for the PI can be optionally provided; Remote Referees use a different three-option recommendation (see separate rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote Referees' funding recommendation options
rubrics_metrics.description: Remote Referees provide a qualitative three-option funding recommendation on the proposal: highly recommended, recommended, or not recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remote Referees are specialists brought in at Step 2; they deliver their assessments by electronic means and do not participate in panel meetings. Their recommendation feeds into the panel's assessment alongside Panel Members' reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual reviews: required elements and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviews must contain explanatory comments for the Research Project and a qualitative assessment for the PI (PI comment optional at Step 2). Reviews must be submitted by ERCEA deadlines. Each proposal shall be reviewed by at least three peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanatory comments for strengths and weaknesses in light of the evaluation criterion; award the numerical mark and PI qualitative assessment; avoid copy-paste; differences of opinion among reviewers are legitimate and will be included in Evaluation Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standards for individual reviewers' comments (Do's)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual reviewers’ comments should be good quality, genuine, substantial, polite, and provide statements and explanations of key strengths and weaknesses in light of the evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide substantial, explanatory comments (avoid mere description/summary); use dispassionate, analytical, unambiguous language; grammatically correct, clear sentences with no jargon; ensure critical comments are constructive; make comments consistent with marks/funding recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited content and behaviours in reviews (Don'ts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must avoid certain types of content and behaviours when writing individual assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid self-declaration of insufficient expertise; avoid dismissive statements about applicant, proposed science, or field; avoid reference to applicant’s age, nationality, gender, personal matters, or Host Institution; avoid direct comparison with other proposals or previous assessments; avoid using surrogate measures (e.g. Journal Impact Factor); avoid comments on ethics or security (these are checked after scientific evaluation); avoid copy-paste from proposal or other reviews; be vigilant about unconscious bias (gender/diversity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and non-contact rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers must not engage in any contact with applicants or beneficiaries about the evaluation they participate in, neither during nor after the evaluation, and must keep proposals confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the individual remote review phase there shall be no discussions of the proposals between reviewers; Panel Members should not disclose assigned proposals to other experts. Breach of Expert Code of Conduct may lead to termination of Contract or appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest: declaration and list of situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts will be shown a list of conflicts in the online system and must confirm absence of conflict when accepting and when submitting reviews; experts are responsible to declare conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed conflict situations include (original wording condensed): 'I am PI or team member; I was involved in preparation; I would benefit from acceptance/rejection; employed/contracted by an entity involved (past 3 years); director/trustee/partner/management involvement (past 3 years); collaborating scientifically in past 5 years; mentor/mentee relationship; family ties or close personal relationship with PI or those involved; relationship of scientific rivalry/hostility; I am National Contact Point or working for EEN; member of an EU programme committee; any other situation that would preclude impartiality.' Panel Chairs avoid assigning reviewers with declared conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel scores and their meanings (A invited / A not invited / B / C)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 1 and Step 2 panels assign categorical scores: Step 1 uses A invited, A not invited, B, C; Step 2 uses A or B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score definitions: 'A invited – proposal is of excellent quality and ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2'; 'A not invited – excellent quality but not ranked sufficiently high to pass to Step 2'; 'B – high quality but not sufficient to pass to Step 2'; 'C – not of sufficient quality to pass to Step 2.' At Step 2: 'A – fully meets ERC excellence and recommended for funding if funds available'; 'B – meets some but not all aspects and not recommended for funding.' Step 1 Bs may be ranked with 10% intervals; some scores (e.g. C at Step1) receive standard panel comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel comment drafting and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead Reviewers draft panel comments reflecting main points of panel discussion; panel agrees and approves final version. Panel comment should explain reasons respecting the ERC evaluation criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel comment should clearly explain the reason(s) making the proposal succeed or fail, be distinct from binding budget recommendations, and at Step 2 take into account the interview. For C scores at Step 1 a standard panel comment is issued. Panel comments must be documented and may include justification for budget cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step evaluation structure and reviewer roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Single submission of full proposals followed by a two-step evaluation: Step 1 remote review of Part B1 (Part I + CV/track record) by Panel Members acting as generalists; Step 2 remote review of full retained proposals (Part B1 and B2) by Panel Members and Remote Referees, followed by interviews and final ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel Members perform familiarisation, individual remote reviews, and participate in panel meetings; Panel Chairs assign proposals, select Remote Referees, chair meetings and ensure deliverables; Remote Referees provide specialist input (typically 2–5 per proposal) at Step 2 and do not attend panel meetings; PEVs support workload where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers must not assess resources or recommend budgets at Step 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid recommendations on resources at Step 1 evaluation; assessment of resources is done at Step 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Step 2 the panel analyses the budget and justification; recommendations for reductions (excluding salaries) may be made if expenses are not fully justified but cuts across-the-board are not allowed. Any recommended budget cut must be documented and explained in the panel comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and salary guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should avoid recommendations on salaries during evaluation, and salary levels are subject to national/institutional rules and are eligible costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a budget cut is recommended at Step 2, provide proper justification based on analysis of resources requested and necessary to carry out the work. Avoid blanket salary recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter- and multi-disciplinary proposal handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter- and multi-disciplinary proposals are encouraged; panels are broad and multidisciplinary and may request additional reviews from other panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's initial panel choice is paramount; applicants may indicate a secondary panel and must justify interdisciplinarity in Part B1. During evaluation interdisciplinary proposals are flagged and panel may request extra reviews; responsibility for fair treatment primarily rests with panels. Panels may reallocate proposals between panels by agreement of both Panel Chairs if expertise requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking and possible voting or cumulative ranking systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Ranking is outcome of panel discussion excluding conflicted Panel Members; while consensus is preferred panels may use voting or cumulative ranking systems to expedite decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting example: majority vote on one or more proposals, each Panel Member one vote per proposal; Panel Chair/Member cannot participate in discussion or vote on a conflicted proposal. Cumulative ranking: Panel Members submit preferred rankings which are added and averaged to produce a cumulative ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publication metrics and research assessment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing research achievements, focus on scientific content and refrain from using surrogate measures such as Journal Impact Factors; quantitative indicators should be used responsibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ERC Scientific Council has endorsed the DORA declaration and signed the Agreement on Reforming Research Assessment; reviewers should prioritise qualitative judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and expected conduct during remote phase
rubrics_metrics.description: During the individual remote review process there shall be no discussions of the proposals between reviewers and Panel Members should not disclose assigned proposals to other experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Panel Member considers they have insufficient expertise to evaluate an assigned proposal, they must inform ERCEA Scientific Officers and the Panel Chair immediately so it can be reassigned. Panel Members are expected to familiarise with all proposals in panel even if they review a subset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverables of panel meetings and feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel meeting deliverables include a panel report with annexes (ranked list, panel comments, list of approved Remote Referees, Conflict of Interest list, and at Step 2 panel recommendations for future evaluations). Evaluation Reports sent to applicants contain recommendation and ranking range, panel comment, and individual reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants rejected at Step 1 receive information letters with Evaluation Report containing final panel score, ranking range, panel comment (or standard comment) and individual reviews. Applicants retained to Step 2 do not receive Step 1 Evaluation Report; after Step 2 all applicants evaluated receive their Evaluation Report including ranking range, panel score, panel comment and individual reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of reviewers per proposal and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC Rules require that each proposal shall be reviewed by at least three peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual reviews must be submitted no later than ERCEA deadlines. Panel Members are expected to deliver concise but substantial reviews and to be available for both panel meetings; Panel Members normally attend on-site evaluation sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of proposals with similar positive reviews but limited slots
rubrics_metrics.description: Some proposals of reasonable or good quality may be rejected due to panel limits (e.g. maximum 44 proposals passed to Step 2) or funding limits; panel comments may reflect this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels should explain in panel comments when a proposal is not advanced due to ranking limits rather than being of inadequate quality. A not invited and C score proposals at Step 1 as well as B score proposals in Step 2 are not ranked within their category and applicants receive a rank range of the entire category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget normalisation and final call ranking (NAB principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: After Step 2, results are consolidated into one call ranking list based on the 'normalised accumulated budget' (NAB) taking into account proposal rank, recommended budget and panel indicative budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended NAB for a panel is calculated by summing normalised budgets (recommended budget divided by panel's indicative budget) from the top down. Highest ranked A scored proposals are invited for grant preparation until call budget is spent; remaining recommended proposals may be funded if additional funds become available.
